facts.intro: A sturdy handle extends from the top of the grinder, ready for a thumb to grasp and rotate.
facts.reveal: Turning the handle rotates a large central gear that sits inside the grinder’s body.
facts.step1: The big gear’s teeth engage with a smaller side gear attached to the burr set.
facts.step2: As the side gear turns, it drives the burrs to rotate in opposite directions.
facts.step3: The rotating burrs crush coffee beans caught between them into a fine grind.
facts.step4: The ground coffee falls out through a chute at the bottom while the handle continues to spin.
facts.hold: If you stop turning, the gears lock together, holding the burrs in place and keeping the beans from moving.
facts.payoff: The simple gear train lets a single hand motion efficiently grind beans without electricity.
